debate.text: Corvenhall wants 300 young people back in learning and has money for 120. Every answer crossed a red line: shut the adult evening classes, spend the savings, or give the extra 180 two hours of maths with volunteers. The jury kept every line, 6 to 4. I sent it back. A child would notice being let in, then let down.

Grace, the jury chose 120 funded places. That leaves 180 young people on a list, and I know where lists like that end up. A lad of seventeen with nothing to do in January is a lad on the dole at nineteen. The town should rethink the funder's cap, not the college's savings.
Callum is right to worry. Young people out of school and out of work are the ones we see in the figures later. I cannot prove the link from one made-up town, but I would not bet against it.
Then say it plainly to the funder. Pay for the places the town needs, or tell us which 180 do not get one. I will not pretend volunteers are teachers.
